text:
incident-bot: P1 PAGE -> Enterprise customer 'AcmeAnalytics' reporting streaming 504s and websocket disconnects via their app gateway to our Dedicated pool dp-11 (VPC). Auto-created incident. Runbook: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/streaming-gateway-timeouts>. Paging Erin (oncall).

erin (oncall): Acknowledged. Jumping in. Marta, what is Acme seeing? Any recent deploys or config changes on their side?

marta (customer-success): They reported failures starting ~09:12 UTC after an internal change to their gateway (NGINX). Symptoms: intermittent 504s on long-lived streams (>15s), client-observed websocket disconnects. They saw logs from their gateway noting `upstream prematurely closed connection`.

dave (sre): Looking at Redwood proxy logs: spikes of `client_disconnected` and connection resets proxied to runtime-dp11 between 09:11-09:16. Example snippet: ```
2026-03-15T09:13:02Z proxy-pool-3 connection reset from 10.2.5.12: downstream closed
2026-03-15T09:13:02Z runtime-dp11 pod-7f client_disconnected stream_id=8
```

kevin (infra): On our side, the route for that tenant has an Envoy/NGINX upstream idle timeout 30s by default. If Acme's gateway is closing earlier or has no keepalives, streams can be torn down. Marta, can you confirm the gateway timeout value?

marta (customer-success): Confirmed with the Acme infra lead: they set `proxy_read_timeout` to 30s yesterday to address other issues. They didn't realize streaming would be impacted.

li (runtime): Runtime behavior: long-poll / streaming endpoints rely on periodic bytes or explicit keepalives to keep the TCP connection considered active by intermediate proxies. If no bytes are sent within their timeout window, the proxy will close the connection and upstream will surface as upstream closed prematurely. Mitigation options: 1) temporary per-tenant injected keepalive chunks from our runtime, 2) ask the customer to increase their proxy timeout to >=90s, 3) adjust upstream LB timeouts. Which orders of operations do we want?

erin (oncall): Dual-track: short-term runtime keepalive for tenant to stop immediate failures, and request Acme raise their gateway timeout as a longer-term fix. Li, can you stage a tenant-scoped keepalive? Dave/Kevin, coordinate with Marta to get the customer to adjust NGINX.

li (runtime): I'll add a per-tenant config flag `stream_keepalive_interval` and enable it for acme-42 with interval 10s. This will inject zero-length chunk keepalives every 10s while the stream is idle. I'll canary it to a single pod in dp-11 first. Deploy id will be posted.

kevin (infra): Drafting recommended NGINX snippet for Acme to apply: ```
proxy_http_version 1.1;
proxy_set_header Connection "";
proxy_buffering off;
proxy_read_timeout 90s;
proxy_send_timeout 90s;
chunked_transfer_encoding on;
```
Also recommend they disable buffering for streaming endpoints.

marta (customer-success): Sending to Acme now. They replied they'll try increasing to 60s first and report back in ~20m.

dave (sre): While that runs, reducing tenant concurrency on dp-11 to relieve pressure: `rctl set tenant acme-42 max_streams=20`. Executed.

incident-bot: Deploy started: runtime keepalive feature -> canary on dp-11 pod-7f (deploy-7810). Link: <https://redwood.internal/deploys/deploy-7810>

li (runtime): Canary running on pod-7f with `stream_keepalive_interval=10s` for tenant acme-42. Logs showing keepalive injects: ```
2026-03-15T09:23:10Z runtime-dp11 pod-7f stream_keepalive tenant=acme-42 seq=1
2026-03-15T09:23:20Z runtime-dp11 pod-7f stream_keepalive tenant=acme-42 seq=2
```

dave (sre): Early metrics look good. `stream.errors.504{tenant=acme-42}` decreased from ~12/min to ~1-2/min within 6 minutes of canary. Pinning dashboard: <https://redwood.internal/dashboards/stream-errors?tenant=acme-42>

erin (oncall): Keep monitoring for 30m. If stable, promote to all dp-11 pods. Marta, have Acme run their smoke tests.

marta (customer-success): Acme ran a 20-request streaming smoke at 09:35 UTC: all succeeded. They also agreed to set `proxy_read_timeout` to 90s and will apply it; ETA ~10-20m.

support-bot: Created external-facing support ticket RW-INC-2026-119 to track customer comms and remediation guidance.

kevin (infra): Note: We kept tenant isolation — only acme-42 had keepalive enabled. Also temporarily adjusted routing to prefer eu-west-1 replicas for acme-42 while we assessed impact.

li (runtime): Promoting canary to full dp-11 pool now: `redwood deploy promote --deploy-id deploy-7810 --pool dp-11 --tenant acme-42`. Rolling.

dave (sre): Roll completed at 09:47 UTC. Post-roll metrics: `stream.errors.504{tenant=acme-42}` ~0.2/min. Traces show keepalive bytes every 10s and no premature upstream closes.

erin (oncall): Handoff to daytime oncall (kevin) in 20 minutes. Erin -> Kevin: ensure Acme applied NGINX change, keep the keepalive enabled for at least 24h, capture traces for full RCA.

kevin (infra): Acknowledged. Action list: 1) Confirm Acme applied proxy_read_timeout=90s (marta). 2) Keep runtime keepalive active 24h (li). 3) Monitor perf/cost (dave). 4) Draft postmortem and customer note (marta/erin).

marta (customer-success): Acme confirmed proxy_read_timeout=90s at 10:05 UTC. They report no failed streams on follow-up tests.

dave (sre): No regressions across other tenants. dp-11 CPU increase ~1-2% due to extra keepalive writes, within acceptable bounds. Keeping monitoring pinned.

erin (oncall): Closing my paging loop. Incident remains open for postmortem. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

kevin (infra): Marking mitigation successful. Filing postmortem RW-PM-2026-019 and collecting artifacts: timeline, logs, deploys, customer comms.

incident-bot: Incident status -> Mitigated. Follow-ups: RW-INC-2026-119, RW-PM-2026-019. Re-open if recurrence observed.
